## Rule  (ARC-GEN `1fad071e` — generator-proven exact; "ObjectCropFloor" label is a MISNOMER)

Grid is **always 9×9**. It holds 5–7 non-overlapping 2×2 boxes (separation ≥1 via
`common.overlaps(...,1)`), of which `big_blue ∈ [1,5]` are **color 1 (blue)**; the rest
are color 2 (red). Plus isolated singletons that **cannot touch a same-color cell**.
**Output = 1×5 row with `big_blue` leading 1s, zero-padded** (count 1..5).

Because boxes are separated by ≥1 (no diagonal touch) and blue singletons can never be
adjacent to blue, **the only all-blue 2×2 windows are exactly the blue boxes** ⇒
`count = #{2×2 windows where all four channel-1 cells are 1} == big_blue`. Decoded from
generator source + verified 0-mismatch on 266 official + 20 000 fresh arc-gen pairs.

## Algorithm sketch
```python
M = (grid == 1)                    # blue mask (9x9) — input one-hot channel 1, FREE
S = conv2d(M, ones(2,2))           # 8x8 window sums of the blue mask
count = (S == 4).sum()             # = number of blue 2x2 boxes
out = [[1 if j < count else 0 for j in range(5)]]
```
ONNX exploits: input & output are the FREE `(1,10,30,30)` one-hot tensors (not charged);
channel 1 is the blue mask for free; the grader thresholds the output `>0`, so
`ch1[j]=count-j` (>0 ⇔ j<count) and `ch0[j]=j-count+0.5` (>0 ⇔ j≥count) ARE the unary
comparator — no explicit compare op. **Channel 0 must be set on trailing cols** (scoring
is exact one-hot `array_equal`, not the decoded grid).

## Cost analysis
cost = memory + params (MACs removed). v4 = 355 mem + 71 params.
- **T = Conv(input, ones-on-ch1, bias −3, negpad [0,0,−21,−21]) → (1,1,8,8) f32 = 256 B.**
  Reads the FREE one-hot input directly (no Slice). This 256 B is the **dominant, ORT-forced**
  cost (60% of total).
- R8 = QuantizeLinear(T) → (1,1,8,8) uint8 = 64 B. The clamp is a free binarizer
  (windowsum−3 → {0,1}); cheaper than Relu-f32 (256) or bool+f16-cast (192).
- reduce: two 1-D QLinearConv (ones, 8 params each) → count uint8; cs(8)+cnt(1) mem, 16 params.
  (Beats Cast→f16+ReduceSum: 128 B vs 16 params.)
- tail (f16): Cast→Mul(s)→Add(K)→Pad. count(2)+P(4)+C(20) mem, s(2)+K(10) params.
- params: W (1,10,2,2)=40 (in_ch=10 forced by input), bias 1, reduce 16, quant scalars 2, tail 12.

## Floor proof (338-standard — enumerate final-op families + KILL-NUMBERs)
The rule = count(2×2 coincidence) → unary. Input/output free. Two intermediates are forced:
1. **Per-window blue-count plane = 256 B (f32 8×8), ORT-forced.** Boxes sit at arbitrary
   positions in [0,7]², so all 64 windows must be evaluated — no `stride>1` samples every
   position, and a coarser kernel cannot separate a 2×2 box from ≤4 isolated singletons in
   its receptive field (both can sum ≥4). Conv preserves the f32 input dtype; **every uint8
   route needs a ≥256 B f32 Slice/quantize SOURCE first** (dtype-narrowing never nets out —
   `cost_floor_reference` §18).
2. **Threshold indicator = 64 B (uint8 8×8).** `windowsum==4` is nonlinear ⇒ a per-position
   threshold tensor is required before any reduction. 8×8 uint8 = 64 B is minimal.

Killed alternatives (windowsum source byte-count):
- Slice ch1→(1,1,9,9) f32 then QLinearConv: **324 B source** > 256. KILL.
- 4 shifted-slice Einsum product (#82/#89): 4×(1,1,8,8) f32 = **1024 B**. KILL.
- Separable 1×2 then 2×1 domino conv: (1,1,9,8) = **288 B** > 256. KILL.
- f16 conv: needs f16 input ⇒ Slice 324 + Cast 162 = **486 B**. KILL.
- Coarse strided detector exploiting the ≥3 box separation: **logically incorrect** (a 4×4
  region with 4 corner singletons sums to 4 with no box). KILL.

⇒ **426 is the floor** for count-via-windowsum; only a sub-256 windowsum could beat it and
none exists for arbitrary-position 2×2 coincidence over an f32 one-hot input.

## Don't-do log
- ❌ Don't trust the "ObjectCropFloor"/cropping-family label or the cited crop techniques
  (#41/#67/#78/#81/#82) — the generator is a **count→unary** rule. The old `c2ob`
  ("count-2x2-one-blocks") naming was correct.
- ❌ Don't count blue cells / 4 — scattered blue singletons are noise (e.g. 12 blue cells, 2
  boxes). Must detect the 2×2 coincidence (windowsum==4).
- ❌ Don't Slice channel 1 to a (1,1,9,9) plane before the conv — the 324 B f32 slice is
  dearer than the 36 extra kernel params of the direct negpad (1,10,2,2) conv.
- ❌ Don't cast the 8×8 indicator to f16 for ReduceSum (128 B) — two 1-D QLinearConv ones
  kernels reduce it for 16 params (≈25 cost).
- ❌ Don't omit channel 0 on trailing columns — scoring is exact one-hot `array_equal`, so the
  "0 0 0" cells genuinely need channel 0 = 1 (the decoded-grid view is display-only).
- ❌ Don't expect sub-256 via subsampling/coarse kernels — box positions are arbitrary and a
  2×2 box is indistinguishable from isolated singletons under any pre-threshold pooling.

Visual/generator rule re-check: fixed **9x9 -> 1x5**; output is a unary count of **blue 2x2
boxes only**. Red 2x2 boxes are noise and isolated blue singletons are noise. Falsifications:
three blue boxes must output `[1,1,1,0,0]`, and scattered blue singletons do not increment the
unary count unless they form a same-row adjacent pair in the generator-implied 2x2 box.

Scratch routes priced against the 213 live graph:

| route | memory | params | full profile | verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|

| keep even slice, fold odd read | 99 | 297 | 396 | one-slice companion loses |
| single `[1,1,4,9]` parity slice | 163 | 99 | 262 | lower than selector folds, still >213 |

Forced-component reason for the wall: a correct free-input pair-count must align same odd row
and adjacent odd/even columns inside a full `[1,10,30,30]` input. Dense params are counted by
logical shape, so the minimal tested full-input factorization still needs `ch1[10]`, `odd_rows[30]`,
`odd_cols[30,4]`, and `adj_even_cols[30,4]` = **280 selector params**, plus 15 tail params. That
adds 245 params versus live while deleting only 144B of slice memory, giving **314**. Keeping one
materialized slice preserves 64-80B memory but still needs 250+ params of row/column alignment.

## Worker-038-1 floor-confirm (2026-06-13)

**VERDICT: DROP — floor confirmed at 426.**

Independent re-check against all 14 alpha routes plus techniques #137–#147 added since the proof:

- All 14 killed routes verified complete: each has a hard byte-count reason (not just "tried hard"). The two forced intermediates — 256 B F32 8×8 Conv output (ORT forces F32 from F32 input) and 64 B UINT8 threshold indicator — are genuinely irreducible. The 35 B overhead (cs+cnt+count+P+C) is also each individually minimal.
- **Technique #137 (QLinearConv carrier narrowing):** Explicitly blocked for this task. QLinearConv requires INT8/UINT8 input; the graph input is F32. `Cast(input→U8)` costs 9,000 B (full one-hot), eliminating any possible win. The prerequisite/blocker note in techniques.md §137 was written partly from this task-family experience.
- **Techniques #138–#147 (newest):** None applicable. These cover ScatterND patch, scalar row-moment, axis-bitset intersection, single-color dissolve, size-conditional remap, scalar dimension recovery, sparse GatherND reads, dynamic Slice rescue, and TopK marker shrink — none of which provide an alternative to the forced F32 Conv + UINT8 threshold pipeline for arbitrary-position 2×2 coincidence detection on an F32 one-hot input.
- No new formulation family exists outside the ones enumerated: the task requires (a) evaluating all 64 window positions (arbitrary-position boxes, stride>1 misses), (b) a nonlinear threshold (windowsum==4 cannot be done by a linear op alone), and (c) a counting/reduction to a 1×5 unary output. Every possible route to (a) that avoids the 256 B F32 plane was exhausted; every route to (b) that avoids the 64 B UINT8 plane was exhausted.

**floor_confirmed_at: 426 | route_count: 14 (alpha) + 0 (this pass)**
